source: QuickHatch curated compatibility overrides for common Windows apps, unsupported vendor tools, and high-value migration targets.

entries.name: Adobe Creative Cloud
entries.notes: Adobe Creative Cloud desktop apps are not officially supported on Linux. Keep Windows/VM or use alternatives.

entries.name: Adobe Photoshop
entries.notes: No official Linux build. Wine support is unreliable for modern Adobe releases.

entries.name: Adobe Illustrator
entries.notes: No official Linux build. Inkscape is the closest native vector workflow.

entries.name: Adobe Premiere Pro
entries.notes: No official Linux build. DaVinci Resolve is the strongest native professional replacement.

entries.name: Adobe After Effects
entries.notes: No official Linux build. There is no exact drop-in replacement.

entries.name: Adobe Lightroom
entries.notes: No official Linux build. Native RAW-photo workflows exist but differ.

entries.name: Microsoft Office
entries.notes: No supported native Microsoft Office desktop suite for Linux. Web apps or compatible office suites are the practical path.

entries.name: Microsoft OneDrive
entries.notes: No official Linux sync client. Third-party clients work but need explicit account setup.

entries.name: Microsoft Teams
entries.notes: Use the web/PWA experience on Linux unless a distro-specific package is confirmed.

entries.name: Microsoft Visual Studio
entries.notes: Full Visual Studio IDE is Windows/macOS only. Linux workflows need different IDEs/toolchains.

entries.name: Microsoft Power BI Desktop
entries.notes: Power BI Desktop is Windows-only. Use web/service or alternatives.

entries.name: SQL Server Management Studio
entries.notes: SSMS is Windows-only. Azure Data Studio and DBeaver are native Linux options.

entries.name: Xbox app
entries.notes: The Windows Xbox/Game Pass app is not available on Linux. Some games work through other stores or cloud streaming.

entries.name: Microsoft PowerToys
entries.notes: PowerToys is Windows-only, but most features have Linux desktop equivalents.

entries.name: iTunes
entries.notes: Modern iTunes is not a native Linux app.

entries.name: iCloud for Windows
entries.notes: No full official Linux iCloud desktop sync suite.

entries.name: NVIDIA App
entries.notes: Windows NVIDIA utilities do not migrate. Linux uses driver packages plus nvidia-settings/nvidia-smi.

entries.name: AMD Software: Adrenalin Edition
entries.notes: Windows Adrenalin does not migrate. Linux AMD graphics normally use Mesa/amdgpu.

entries.name: ASUS Armoury Crate
entries.notes: Windows vendor utility does not migrate. Linux support depends heavily on model.

entries.name: MSI Center
entries.notes: Windows vendor utility does not migrate. Avoid guessing hardware-control replacements.

entries.name: Corsair iCUE
entries.notes: Official iCUE is not available for Linux. Device support varies by model.

entries.name: Razer Synapse
entries.notes: Official Synapse is not available for Linux. OpenRazer supports many devices.

entries.name: Logitech G HUB
entries.notes: Official G HUB is not available for Linux. Device support depends on the exact hardware.

entries.name: SteelSeries GG
entries.notes: Official Linux support is limited; audio/RGB/device features vary.

entries.name: Elgato Stream Deck
entries.notes: Official Stream Deck app is not native Linux; community tools exist.

entries.name: NZXT CAM
entries.notes: Official CAM is not native Linux. Cooling/RGB support depends on hardware.

entries.name: Lenovo Vantage
entries.notes: Windows vendor app does not migrate. Firmware/power settings use Linux-native tools.

entries.name: Dell SupportAssist
entries.notes: Windows vendor app does not migrate. Firmware updates usually use fwupd/LVFS.

entries.name: HP Support Assistant
entries.notes: Windows vendor app does not migrate. Printers use HPLIP; firmware uses fwupd when supported.

entries.name: Google Drive for desktop
entries.notes: No official Google Drive desktop sync client for Linux.

entries.name: Dropbox
entries.notes: Dropbox provides Linux packages, but install method varies by distro.

entries.notes: Native Linux client exists. Do not enable/start VPN automatically unless the user explicitly asks.

ubuntu.notes: Use Mullvad's current vendor repository/package instructions; do not activate VPN/firewall without explicit confirmation.

fedora.notes: Use Mullvad's current vendor repository/package instructions; do not activate VPN/firewall without explicit confirmation.

entries.notes: Native Linux app exists.

entries.name: Notepad++

entries.name: Everything
entries.notes: Everything is Windows-only. FSearch is the closest native GUI replacement.

entries.name: ShareX
entries.notes: ShareX is Windows-only; Linux screenshot tools cover most use cases.

entries.name: Rufus
entries.notes: Rufus is Windows-only; Linux has multiple bootable-media tools.

entries.name: WinRAR

entries.name: WinSCP
entries.notes: Linux file managers and CLI tools handle SFTP/SCP well.

entries.name: Steam
entries.notes: Steam is the main Linux gaming launcher; enable Proton for Windows games.

arch.notes: Arch multilib package.

debian.notes: Install from the distro/vendor-supported Steam package path after confirming repositories.

ubuntu.notes: Install from Ubuntu's current Steam installer package or vendor path after confirming repositories.

fedora.notes: Steam usually requires RPM Fusion/Flatpak; verify current repo setup first.

entries.name: Epic Games Store
entries.notes: Use Heroic or Lutris instead of the Windows launcher.

entries.name: GOG Galaxy
entries.notes: GOG Galaxy itself is Windows-first; Linux users generally use Heroic/Lutris/Minigalaxy.

entries.name: Battle.net
entries.notes: Use Lutris/Bottles; game anti-cheat and launcher updates can break compatibility.

entries.name: EA app
alternatives: Steam Proton for Steam-owned EA games
entries.notes: Use Lutris/Bottles or Steam Proton where applicable.

entries.name: Ubisoft Connect
alternatives: Steam Proton for Steam-owned Ubisoft games
entries.notes: Use Lutris/Bottles or Steam Proton where applicable.

entries.name: Riot Client
alternatives: Keep Windows for Riot anti-cheat titles
entries.notes: Riot anti-cheat makes several titles unsuitable for normal Linux migration.
